newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs close lower on regional falls, apathy.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs close lower on regional falls, apathy.

text.p: Shares on the Lima Stock Exchange lost ground Monday on falls in other larger markets in the region and foreign investor disinterest, brokers said.
They predicted the same tendency would continue Tuesday, unless investors became enthused by the low prices of some stocks.
According to preliminary figures, the bolsa's General Index fell 1.73 percent to 2,017.31 points in Monday's session, while the blue-chip Selective Index fell 1.96 percent to 2,909.77.
"The effect of the fall on the U.S. exchange Friday has dragged the whole region down. The worry now is how the U.S. bolsa gets out of the rut," said Teodosio Arias-Schreiber, of Los Andes brokerage.
He added that local political problems and the economic impact of the El Nino weather phenomenon were now lower priorities for investors on the Lima market.
"Today's fall is mainly due to the region. Brazil was down. Also the fall in zinc prices was a factor," said another broker, who asked not to be named.

Most of the Lima market's leaders fell, with benchmark Telefonica del Peru off 2.21 percent to 6.20 soles on 577,300 shares traded, brewery group UPC Backus slipping 3.40 percent to 3.50 soles on 103,00, and miner Atacocha off 1.61 percent to 2.45 soles.

Among the few stocks to advance, ice-cream and confectionery company D'Onofrio rose 2.08 percent to 0.98 sol on just 25,700 shares traded, food company Alicorp ended up 1.35 percent to 3.75 soles on 63,300, and miner Buenaventura gained 2.63 percent to 19.50 soles.
Miner Volcan continued its volatile ride, slipping 4.11 percent to 21.00 soles on 425,116 shares following last week's sharp ups and downs.
